templeRhythm.title: A Symphony of Devotion
templeRhythm.description: From morning to night, here are the daily temple aartis and Vaishnav mantras sung in all ISKCON Temples Worldwide.

featuredMonth.title: Sri Damodar Ashtakam
featuredMonth.description: In the auspicious month of Kartik, offer the sacred Damodar Ashtakam prayer daily & get the mercy of the Lord.

moods.name: Deep Longing
moods.description: These songs express the heart’s deep desire to remember Krishna and remain connected with Him. They reflect the eagerness of a devotee who longs for the Lord’s presence, association and mercy, keeping Krishna as the center of the heart.

moods.name: Reverence
moods.description: These songs express deep respect and appreciation for the Lord’s greatness, qualities and divine nature. Through them, devotees remember Krishna with honor, gratitude and a heart filled with admiration for His unlimited beauty and mercy.

moods.name: Self Surrender
moods.description: These songs reflect the devotee’s complete dependence on Krishna and willingness to place everything in His care. They express faith, acceptance and the desire to dedicate one’s thoughts, actions and life in the service of the Lord.

moods.name: Teachings & Guidance
moods.description: These songs carry the teachings and realizations shared by great devotees and acharyas. They guide us in understanding the path of bhakti, the importance of devotion and the practices that help us move closer to Krishna.

moods.name: Humility
moods.description: The heart of a humble devotee seeking Krishna’s mercy is beautifully reflected through these songs. They inspire simplicity, sincerity and a spirit of service while reminding devotees of their dependence on the Lord and the importance of approaching Him with devotion.

moods.name: Aspiration
moods.description: These songs express the devotee’s heartfelt desire to grow in devotion and deepen the relationship with Krishna. They reflect the wish to develop spiritual qualities, remain engaged in service and progress further on the path of bhakti.

moods.name: Separation
moods.description: The heartfelt longing to be close to Krishna and experience His presence is beautifully expressed through these songs. They reflect the deep attachment of devotees who constantly remember the Lord and cherish the desire to remain connected with Him through love and devotion.

moods.name: Glorification
moods.description: The names, qualities, forms and divine pastimes of the Lord are beautifully remembered through these songs. They help devotees appreciate Krishna’s unlimited beauty, mercy and spiritual activities with love and devotion, deepening their connection with the Supreme Lord.

categories.name: Dependency
categories.description: These songs reveal the mood of a devotee who completely depends on Krishna’s mercy. They express surrender, faith and the desire to remain under the Lord’s shelter in every situation. Through these prayers, devotees learn to place their trust in Krishna and seek His guidance in life.

categories.name: Glories of the Holy Name
categories.description: The chanting of Krishna’s holy name is the essence of devotional practice. These songs glorify the sweetness, mercy and spiritual power of the holy name. They inspire devotees to chant with faith and remind us that the holy name is always a source of shelter and remembrance.

categories.name: Prayer for Mercy
categories.description: A devotee’s heart naturally turns towards the mercy of Krishna and His devotees. These songs express humility, dependence and a sincere prayer for grace. Through heartfelt words, devotees seek strength to continue on the path of bhakti and remain connected with the service of the Lord.

categories.name: Other
categories.description: From remembering the Lord’s pastimes to offering prayers on special occasions, these songs bring different expressions of devotion to the heart. They help us hear about Krishna, remember His devotees and stay connected with bhakti.

categories.name: Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu
categories.description: These songs and prayers dedicated to Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu reflect His teachings, divine qualities and the path of devotion He shared with the world. Through these devotional expressions, devotees remember Mahaprabhu’s mercy, teachings and love for Krishna while connecting with the spirit of bhakti.

categories.name: Stotram & Ashtakam
categories.description: These beautiful prayers glorify the names, qualities and forms of the Lord through carefully composed verses. Stotrams and ashtakams help devotees meditate with focus and devotion, offering praise and remembrance of Krishna, His expansions and great devotees in a traditional way.

categories.name: Tulasi Songs
categories.description: Tulasi Devi is very dear to Krishna and is worshipped by devotees with love and respect. These songs offer prayers and glorification to Tulasi Devi, expressing gratitude and seeking her blessings to engage in the loving service of Sri Krishna with devotion and sincerity.

categories.name: Pranam Mantras
categories.description: With humility and respect, devotees offer prayers through these sacred mantras before beginning devotional activities. They help us remember the Lord, spiritual master and great devotees while seeking their blessings. These prayers create a proper mood of gratitude, remembrance and devotion as we begin our spiritual practices.

categories.name: Spiritual Master
categories.description: These songs express devotion, gratitude and respect towards the spiritual master, who guides devotees on the path of bhakti. Through prayers and glorification, they help devotees remember the guru’s teachings, mercy and service while seeking inspiration to deepen their connection with Krishna.

categories.name: Shri Nityananada Prabhu
categories.description: The devotion towards Sri Nityananda Prabhu is expressed through heartfelt songs and prayers that reflect His unlimited compassion, mercy and loving nature. These compositions remember His connection with Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and His gift of Krishna consciousness, inspiring devotees to cultivate humility, faith and devotion.

categories.name: Lord Shri Krishna
categories.description: These special songs express devotion towards Sri Krishna by remembering His divine qualities, enchanting form and loving pastimes. Through heartfelt expressions of bhakti, they help devotees deepen their remembrance of Krishna, appreciate His mercy and develop a loving connection with the Supreme Lord.

categories.name: Shrimati Radharani
categories.description: These songs glorify the divine love, qualities and devotion of Srimati Radharani, the eternal beloved of Krishna. Through heartfelt prayers and remembrance, they express the devotee’s desire to seek Her mercy, follow Her mood of devotion and engage in the loving service of Sri Krishna.

categories.name: Narasimha Prayers
categories.description: These prayers remember Lord Narasimha, His powerful form and His loving protection of devotees. They are offered with faith and devotion, seeking shelter at the lotus feet of the Lord. These songs help devotees remember His mercy and divine presence during their spiritual journey.

authors.name: Bhaktivinoda Thakura
authors.description: Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakura is remembered as a great Gaudiya Vaishnava acharya who revived and spread the teachings of Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. His books and devotional collections like Saranagati, Gitavali and Kalyana-kalpataru contain beloved songs such as Jiva Jago, Manasa Deho Geho and Gurudeva Kripa Bindu Diya, expressing humility, surrender and devotion.

authors.name: Narottama Dasa Thakura
authors.description: Srila Narottama Dasa Thakura is remembered as one of the most beloved Gaudiya Vaishnava acharyas and a renowned kirtana composer. His famous works include Prarthana and Prema Bhakti Chandrika. Songs like Hari Hari Bifale and Gauranga Bolite Habe express humility, longing and the desire to attain pure devotion.

authors.name: A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami
authors.description: Srila Prabhupada is remembered for spreading the teachings of Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and Krishna consciousness throughout the world. Along with his translations and books like Bhagavad-gita As It Is and Srimad-Bhagavatam, his devotional songs express surrender, gratitude and dedication to Guru and Krishna. His prayers reflect his desire to serve and share Krishna bhakti.

authors.name: Vrindavana Dasa Thakura
authors.description: Vrindavana Dasa Thakura holds a cherished place in the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition through his writings on the life and teachings of Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. His devotional works also celebrate Sri Nityananda Prabhu and the chanting of the holy name, preserving the deep devotional spirit of the early Gaudiya tradition.

authors.name: Krsnadasa Kaviraja Goswami
authors.description: Krishna Dasa Kaviraja Goswami is one of the most respected Gaudiya Vaishnava acharyas and the author of Sri Chaitanya Charitamrita. His writings describe the life, teachings and mercy of Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. His songs and prayers express deep devotion, humility and appreciation for Gauranga and Krishna.

authors.name: Locana Dasa Thakura
authors.description: Lochana Dasa Thakura was a great Gaudiya Vaishnava poet and devotee, famous for his work Chaitanya Mangala, which describes the life and pastimes of Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. His songs express love for Gauranga, remembrance of His mercy and the joy of chanting the holy name.

authors.name: Adi Sankaracarya
authors.description: Adi Shankaracharya is one of India’s greatest spiritual teachers, known for his commentaries on Vedanta and works like Bhaja Govindam. Among his devotional compositions, Kadacit Kalindi Tata Vipina is remembered for its loving remembrance of Krishna’s pastimes, showing his appreciation for devotional expression.

authors.name: Vasudeva Ghosha
authors.description: Vasudeva Ghosha is remembered as a renowned kirtana composer and devotee associated with the early Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition. His devotional songs celebrate Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, Sri Nityananda Prabhu and Krishna, carrying heartfelt expressions of love, remembrance and devotion through the tradition of congregational chanting.

authors.name: Krishna Dwipayana Vyasadeva
authors.description: Vyasadeva holds a central place in the sacred literature of the Vaishnava tradition and is traditionally regarded as the compiler of the Vedic literature and author of the Srimad Bhagavatam. His works preserve the teachings, pastimes and devotional wisdom centered on the Supreme Lord, providing an important foundation for understanding Krishna bhakti.

authors.name: Rupa Goswami
authors.description: Among the Six Goswamis of Vrindavana, Srila Rupa Goswami holds a central place in shaping the teachings and devotional literature of the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition. His writings, including Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu and Ujjvala-nilamani, explore the depth of Krishna bhakti, devotional love and the service of Sri Radha and Krishna.

authors.name: Sarvabhauma Bhattacarya
authors.description: Sarvabhauma Bhattacarya holds an important place in the life and teachings of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. A renowned scholar of Vedanta, he later became a devoted follower of Mahaprabhu, and his prayers and devotional expressions reflect deep appreciation for Gauranga’s divine nature and mercy.

authors.name: Vishvanatha Cakravarti Thakura
authors.description: Vishvanatha Chakravarti Thakura holds a distinguished place among the later Gaudiya Vaishnava acharyas, known for his profound writings on Krishna bhakti and devotional practice. His works, including Raga-vartma-chandrika and Madhurya-kadambini, offer deep insights into the stages of devotion, spiritual emotions and loving service to Sri Radha and Krishna.

authors.name: Bilvamangala Thakura
authors.description: Bilvamangala Thakura, also known as Lilashuka, is remembered for his celebrated devotional work Krishna Karnamrita, which beautifully describes Krishna’s sweetness, beauty and divine pastimes. His writings express deep love, attraction and loving remembrance of Krishna, establishing him as one of the renowned poets of Krishna bhakti.

authors.name: Jayadeva Goswami
authors.description: Jayadeva Goswami is celebrated as one of the greatest Sanskrit poets and devotees of Lord Krishna. He is famous for Gita Govinda, which beautifully describes the loving pastimes of Sri Radha and Krishna. His compositions carry deep devotional emotions and have inspired generations of devotees through their poetic glorification of divine love.

authors.name: Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati
authors.description: Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakura was a prominent Gaudiya Vaishnava acharya and the founder of Gaudiya Math. Through his writings, teachings and devotional songs like Krishna Hoite Chaturmukha, he emphasized pure devotion, service to Guru and Krishna, and the teachings of Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu.

authors.name: Govinda Dasa Kaviraja
authors.description: Govinda Dasa Kaviraja was a renowned Gaudiya Vaishnava poet famous for his heartfelt songs about Sri Krishna and Sri Radha. His compositions, found in collections like Padavali, express deep devotion, longing and remembrance. His famous song Bhaja Hu Re Mana guides the mind to take shelter of Krishna’s lotus feet.

authors.name: Lord Brahma
authors.description: Lord Brahma, the creator of the universe, is remembered as a great devotee who glorified Lord Krishna through his prayers. His famous Brahma Stuti from Srimad Bhagavatam expresses humility, realization and devotion towards Krishna’s supreme position and divine activities.

authors.name: Lord Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu
authors.description: Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu is the central figure of the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition and is remembered as the embodiment of devotion to Krishna. His teachings inspired the chanting of the holy name throughout the world. Songs about Gauranga glorify His mercy, sankirtana movement and loving devotion towards Krishna.

authors.name: Radha Mohana Dasa
authors.description: Radha Mohana Dasa is remembered as a Vaishnava poet whose devotional compositions express deep appreciation for Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, the Vaishnavas and the path of bhakti. His songs such as Sakala Vaisnava Gosai and Vande Visvambhara Pada Kamalam carry heartfelt prayers, remembrance and devotion, reflecting the spirit of Gaudiya Vaishnava poetry.

authors.name: Raghunatha Dasa Goswami
authors.description: Srila Raghunatha Dasa Goswami stands among the Six Goswamis of Vrindavana and is especially remembered for his intimate devotional prayers and writings centered on Sri Radha and Krishna. His works, including Manah-siksha, Vilapa-kusumanjali and Stavavali, express deep longing for devotional service, remembrance of Vraja and wholehearted dedication to the Divine Couple.

authors.name: Vedanta Desika
authors.description: Vedanta Desika stands among the most celebrated scholars, poets and devotees of the Sri Vaishnava tradition. His extensive writings cover philosophy, devotion and Sanskrit poetry, while his devotional compositions express deep surrender, reverence and loving service to Lord Vishnu and His divine forms.

authors.name: Vidyapati
authors.description: Vidyapati remains celebrated for his lyrical poetry centered on Sri Radha and Krishna, especially the intimate expressions of divine love found in his devotional songs. Writing in Maithili, he shaped a rich tradition of devotional poetry whose sweetness, longing and emotional depth continue to inspire Krishna bhakti.

authors.name: Ananta Dasa Sastri
authors.description: Ananta Dasa Shastri is remembered as a devotional scholar and writer whose works reflect deep spiritual understanding. His compositions carry the mood of remembrance, glorification and devotion, helping devotees connect with the Lord through heartfelt expressions of bhakti.

authors.name: Bhakta Salabega
authors.description: Bhakta Salabega was a great devotee of Lord Jagannatha from Odisha, famous for his heartfelt songs filled with love and longing for Jagannatha. His compositions, especially Ahe Nila Saila, reveal deep devotion and surrender, and remain an important part of Jagannatha’s devotional tradition.

authors.name: Bhishma Deva
authors.description: Bhishma Deva, the great devotee from Mahabharata, is remembered for his heartfelt prayers glorifying Lord Krishna before leaving his body. His famous Bhishma Stuti describes Krishna’s divine form, qualities and mercy, revealing the heart of a devotee fully absorbed in remembrance and devotion to the Lord.

authors.name: Budhakaushika
authors.description: Budhakaushika is traditionally remembered as the composer of Rama Raksha Stotra, a revered Sanskrit prayer dedicated to Lord Rama. The stotra expresses devotion, faith and remembrance of Lord Rama, describing His divine qualities and seeking His protection and grace.

authors.name: Candrasekhara Kavi
authors.description: Candrasekhara Kavi is remembered for devotional poetry centered on the worship of Lord Krishna and Tulasi Devi. His well-known Tulasi Arati expresses reverence for Tulasi Maharani and a heartfelt prayer for pure devotion, reflecting the intimate devotional spirit found in Vaishnava worship.

authors.name: Devakinandana Das Thakura
authors.description: Devakinandana Das Thakura was a Gaudiya Vaishnava poet known for his devotional compositions glorifying Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and His associates. His songs carry the mood of remembrance, devotion and appreciation for Gauranga’s mercy, helping devotees connect with the loving teachings and pastimes of Mahaprabhu.

authors.name: Gopis
authors.description: The Gopis of Vrindavana are remembered as the highest examples of loving devotion to Sri Krishna. Their feelings of love, dedication and constant remembrance are described in scriptures like Srimad Bhagavatam. Songs inspired by the Gopis express deep attachment, longing and the desire to serve Krishna with a selfless heart.

authors.name: Hari Vyasa Devacarya
authors.description: Hari Vyasa Devacarya was a respected Vaishnava acharya and poet known for his devotional compositions dedicated to Lord Krishna. His writings express deep devotion, remembrance and appreciation for the Lord’s divine qualities, reflecting the heartfelt emotions of a devotee absorbed in bhakti.

authors.name: Jagannatha Dasa
authors.description: Jagannatha Dasa is remembered as a great Odia devotee and author of Odia Bhagavata, a beloved presentation of Srimad Bhagavatam in the Odia language. His devotional works express faith, surrender and love for Lord Krishna, making him one of the important figures in Odisha’s devotional tradition.

authors.name: Jiva Goswami
authors.description: Srila Jiva Goswami was one of the prominent Gaudiya Vaishnava acharyas and a great philosopher of the tradition. His famous works include the Sat Sandarbhas, which present the teachings of Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu in detail. His writings and prayers reflect deep understanding of Krishna bhakti and devotion.

authors.name: Kanu Ramadasa Thakura
authors.description: Kanu Ramadasa Thakura was a devotee and poet in the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition known for devotional compositions glorifying Sri Krishna and Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. His songs carry expressions of remembrance, devotion and love for the Lord, following the mood of surrender found in Vaishnava poetry.

authors.name: Kulasekhara Alvar
authors.description: Kulashekhara Alvar was one of the great Vaishnava saints of the Sri Vaishnava tradition. He is best known for works like Mukunda Mala Stotra, a beautiful collection of prayers that glorify Lord Krishna. His compositions express surrender, devotion and a strong desire to always remember the Lord’s lotus feet.

authors.name: Kusakratha Dasa
authors.description: Kusakratha Dasa is remembered for his scholarship, translations, and dedication to making important Sanskrit and Bengali Vaishnava literature accessible to devotees. As a disciple of Srila Prabhupada, he translated numerous works of great Vaishnava acharyas, helping readers explore their teachings, prayers and devotional expressions.

authors.name: Lord Shiva
authors.description: Lord Shiva is honored in Vaishnava tradition as a great devotee of Lord Krishna. His prayers and glorifications, such as those found in Srimad Bhagavatam, reveal his devotion and appreciation for the Supreme Lord. He is remembered as a guide and well-wisher of devotees.

authors.name: Madhvacharya
authors.description: Madhvacharya is remembered as a great spiritual teacher and the founder of the Dvaita Vedanta tradition. His important works include Brahma Sutra Bhashya along with prayers glorifying Lord Vishnu. His teachings emphasize devotion, surrender and the eternal relationship between the soul and the Supreme Lord.

authors.name: Narahari Sarakara
authors.description: Narahari Sarakara Thakura was an associate of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and a respected Gaudiya Vaishnava poet. He is remembered for devotional songs glorifying Gauranga and Krishna. His compositions express deep affection for Mahaprabhu, remembrance of His qualities and loving devotion towards the Lord.

authors.name: Nilakanta Goswami
authors.description: Nilakanta Goswami is remembered as a Vaishnava devotee and poet whose devotional compositions express love, remembrance, and dedication to the Lord. His works reflect the devotional spirit of Vaishnava poetry, offering heartfelt expressions of bhakti and appreciation for the divine.

authors.name: Prabodhananda Sarasvati
authors.description: Prabodhananda Sarasvati was a great devotee and spiritual teacher associated with Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. He is famous for works like Chaitanya Chandrodya Nataka and Sri Radha Rasa Sudhanidhi. His writings glorify Sri Gauranga and Srimati Radharani with deep devotion and appreciation for their divine qualities.

authors.name: Prahalad Maharaj
authors.description: Prahlada Maharaja, one of the twelve Mahajanas, stands among the most beloved devotees of Lord Krishna, remembered for his unwavering faith and devotion from childhood. His prayers in Srimad Bhagavatam express humility, compassion and complete dedication to the Lord, offering timeless inspiration on the path of pure bhakti.

authors.name: Sanatana Goswami
authors.description: Srila Sanatana Goswami made a lasting contribution to the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition through his teachings, writings and guidance on devotional life. As one of the Six Goswamis of Vrindavana, his works such as Brihad-Bhagavatamrita and Hari-bhakti-vilasa provide insights into Krishna bhakti, spiritual practice and the principles of devotional service.

authors.name: Satyavrata Muni
authors.description: Satyavrata Muni is especially remembered for the Damodarashtakam, the eight-verse prayer describing Lord Krishna’s childhood pastimes as Damodara. The prayer beautifully recalls Mother Yashoda’s loving relationship with Krishna and expresses the devotee’s desire for His remembrance and pure devotional service, making it a cherished prayer during Kartika.

authors.name: Shani Deva
authors.description: Shani Deva appears in devotional tradition through prayers that remember his position among the Navagrahas and his connection with Lord Narasimha. His devotional composition Sulabho Bhakti Yuktanam presents prayers offered to Lord Narasimha, expressing faith in His mercy and protection and highlighting Shani Deva’s devotion to the Supreme Lord.

authors.name: Srinivasa Acharya
authors.description: Srinivasa Acarya is remembered as a great Gaudiya Vaishnava devotee and poet, closely connected with the Six Goswamis of Vrindavana. His devotional expressions reflect deep appreciation for their teachings, devotion and service to Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, while inspiring remembrance of the devotional path established by these great acharyas.

authors.name: Svarupa Damodara Goswami
authors.description: Svarupa Damodara Goswami held a close place in the personal pastimes of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and served as His intimate associate in Puri. Known for his deep understanding of scripture, poetry and devotional principles, he carefully examined literary works offered to Mahaprabhu and expressed profound devotion through songs and prayers.

authors.name: Vadiraja Tirtha
authors.description: Vadiraja Tirtha holds an important place in the Madhva tradition as a respected saint, scholar, and poet. His devotional writings and prayers reflect deep devotion to Lord Vishnu, along with appreciation for the Lord’s divine qualities and the path of bhakti.

authors.name: Vallabhacarya
authors.description: Vallabhacharya is remembered as the founder of the Pushtimarga tradition and a respected teacher of Shuddhadvaita Vedanta. His writings and devotional prayers center on loving service to Sri Krishna, especially in His childlike form, and emphasize divine grace, devotion and a personal relationship with the Lord.
